hints.title: Degree Bound Availability
hints.text: Every garden has at most 3 paths connected to it. Because there are 4 distinct flower varieties, a valid unused color always exists for each garden.

hints.title: Neighbor Color Inspection
hints.text: Construct an adjacency list for all gardens. When visiting garden i, check the flower choices already assigned to its neighbors.

hints.title: Greedy First Available Color
hints.text: Iterate gardens from 1 to n. Identify used neighbor flower types in {1, 2, 3, 4}. Assign the smallest available flower variety to garden i.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Full graph coloring backtracking takes exponential time and is unnecessary because max degree is 3.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Greedy sequential assignment guarantees a valid 4-coloring in linear O(N + E) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that max degree <= 3 with 4 colors allows an immediate greedy assignment.
complexity.notes: Each garden degree is bounded by 3, so E <= 1.5 * N.
